title: Inbound operations metric contract
authority: Current Inbound Dashboard and Inbound Data Dictionary; supersedes earlier inline inbound definitions
queue_scope: All enumerated STANDARD queues, or one explicitly selected standard queue. This scope does not claim to count unqueued IVR exits.
time_basis: Amazon contact-record reporting interval (disconnect-date attribution); not an initiation-date cohort. Agent-offer metrics use agent activity events. Preserve the native attribution; never substitute CONTACTS_HANDLED_CONNECTED_TO_AGENT_TIME.

amazon.pagination: Follow every NextToken; split hourly requests into at most two-day windows. Do not turn a missing Collection, Value, or failed request into zero.

warehouse.grain: One native metric result per instance, metric/filters/threshold, queue scope, channel, interval period, start, end and timezone
warehouse.join: Join registry.metric_id to fact.metric_id; queue dimension by instance_id + queue_id only for queue-grouped results. Never fan out an all-queue aggregate to queue rows.
warehouse.sql: SELECT metric_value FROM ANALYTICS_CONNECT.FCT_METRIC_RESULT WHERE metric_id = :metric_id AND request_hash = :request_hash AND status = 'available' QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY instance_id, metric_id, queue_scope_hash, channel, interval_period, interval_start_utc, interval_end_utc, timezone, contract_version ORDER BY retrieved_at_utc DESC) = 1
warehouse.refresh: Local server performs read-only pulls on Apply. Immutable raw responses by request hash + retrieval timestamp; transactional MERGE latest complete result on the full key. Repeat recent completed days for late records. No Snowflake connection is currently asserted.
warehouse.aggregation: Counts: sum complete disjoint intervals only. Rates, averages and maxima: request native TOTAL for selected window, never average hourly values. Heatmap uses sum of hourly counts by ET weekday/hour; missing hours stay unavailable. Repeated DST hours are summed; no synthetic allocation.
tests: all hourly count cells reconcile to same-window native TOTAL
derived operands share envelope and interval

metrics.label: Incoming calls · primary
metrics.meaning: Original inbound voice contact legs in the selected queue reporting scope. A repeat caller can create another leg. The window follows Amazon historical reporting, not necessarily the time the caller first dialed.
metrics.action: Use the daily and hourly pattern to plan queue coverage.

metrics.label: Answered calls · primary
metrics.meaning: Original inbound legs that connected to an agent, reported using Amazon's contact-record interval. Transfer-created legs are excluded.
metrics.action: Read with primary incoming and primary abandonment in the same reporting scope.

metrics.label: Not answered · primary
metrics.meaning: Provisional arithmetic remainder: primary created minus primary handled using identical API filters and dates. Amazon assistant disputed the CREATED time basis; therefore this is not yet a verified not-answered outcome population. It is not a unique-caller count or a callback list. Matching arithmetic alone does not resolve cohort attribution.
metrics.action: Investigate abandonment first; use contact records to identify the remaining outcomes.

metrics.label: Incoming legs · all origins
metrics.meaning: Primary inbound plus transfer-created and queue-transfer-created voice legs. A transferred customer can contribute multiple legs.
metrics.action: Use this for incoming workload; use primary incoming for original legs.

metrics.label: Incoming legs · via transfer
metrics.meaning: New voice contact legs whose native initiation method is TRANSFER.
metrics.action: Review transfer demand and receiving-team coverage.

metrics.label: Incoming legs · via queue transfer
metrics.meaning: New voice contact legs whose native initiation method is QUEUE_TRANSFER.
metrics.action: Review routing between queues.

metrics.label: Answered incoming legs · all origins
metrics.meaning: Amazon Contacts handled incoming: includes answered primary, transfer, and queue-transfer legs. CONTACTS_HANDLED_INCOMING is a legacy GetMetricData name, not the V2 identifier.
metrics.action: Use for answered incoming workload across original and successor legs.

metrics.label: Abandoned in queue · all origins
metrics.meaning: Voice contact legs abandoned while queued before agent connection, across every initiation method eligible for the native metric. Amazon applies callback, successor-contact and transfer exclusions.
metrics.action: Locate high-loss queues and staffing windows.

metrics.label: Abandoned in queue · primary
metrics.meaning: The native queue-abandon metric restricted to original INBOUND legs. It does not mean this person has never called previously.
metrics.action: Review first-contact queue wait and callback options.

metrics.label: Abandoned in queue · non-primary
metrics.meaning: All eligible non-INBOUND abandonment: total native abandoned minus its native INBOUND subset. This is not automatically transfer-only; other eligible initiation methods may contribute.
metrics.action: Investigate origin and routing before attributing all loss to transfers.

metrics.label: Queued contacts
metrics.meaning: Voice legs with a queue entry, counted in the disconnect reporting interval. All eligible origins, not just primary inbound. This is not the current waiting queue.
metrics.action: Read with abandonment rate, service level and wait times.

metrics.label: Queue abandonment rate
metrics.meaning: Amazon's native percentage of queued voice contacts abandoned. The denominator is eligible queued contacts, not primary incoming.
metrics.action: Compare like-for-like queue windows; investigate rising loss.

metrics.label: Service level · under 20 sec
metrics.meaning: Amazon's native share of queued contacts removed from queue in less than 20 seconds, including answered, abandoned and callback removals under Amazon eligibility. This is not simply the percentage answered within 20 seconds.
metrics.action: Use alongside abandonment and answer speed. Configure a local target before calling it a breach.

metrics.label: Average speed of answer
metrics.meaning: Average queue wait before agent connection for answered eligible voice contacts. Excludes callers who abandon; read with abandonment time.
metrics.action: Check peak waiting windows and available staffing.

metrics.label: Average wait before abandonment
metrics.meaning: Average queue duration for contacts included in Amazon queue abandonment.
metrics.action: Compare with answer speed to understand whether customers leave before typical answer time.

metrics.label: Maximum historical queue wait
metrics.meaning: Longest eligible queue duration in this historical period. It is not the oldest contact currently waiting.
metrics.action: Investigate long-tail waits even when the average looks acceptable.

metrics.label: Answered in under 20 sec
metrics.meaning: Native cumulative count of eligible queued voice contacts answered after less than 20 seconds in queue.
metrics.action: Use as an answer-speed count; do not substitute it for native service level.

metrics.label: Queue abandons · under 5 sec
metrics.meaning: Cumulative all-origin queue abandons with queue duration strictly below 5 seconds. Includes Amazon's native threshold exclusions; not restricted to primary inbound.
metrics.action: Inspect very short disconnects and routing experience.

metrics.label: Queue abandons · under 20 sec
metrics.meaning: Cumulative all-origin queue abandons with queue duration strictly below 20 seconds. Includes under-5-second abandons; never add these two rows.
metrics.action: Use with average abandon wait to separate early exits from long waits.

metrics.label: Average handle time · all voice
metrics.meaning: Amazon's average handling duration across all eligible voice origins in the selected queues, including interaction, applicable hold and after-contact work (and applicable pause). Excludes pre-answer queue wait. The API rejects an INBOUND metric filter for this field; this is explicitly all-voice context.
metrics.action: Balance efficiency with resolution and customer experience; shorter is not always better.

metrics.label: Average interaction time · primary
metrics.meaning: Agent interaction duration on primary inbound legs, excluding hold and after-contact work.
metrics.action: Review with wrap-up and hold time; do not add independently averaged components as a guaranteed AHT identity.

metrics.label: After-contact work · primary
metrics.meaning: Average wrap-up time after a primary inbound interaction ends.
metrics.action: Look for documentation and workflow friction.

metrics.label: Average customer hold · all voice
metrics.meaning: Average hold duration across eligible held voice contacts in the selected queues. Queue wait before answer is excluded. The API rejects an INBOUND metric filter for this field; this is all-voice context.
metrics.action: Review knowledge gaps and escalation delays.

metrics.label: Placed on hold · primary
metrics.meaning: Primary inbound legs with at least one hold, counted as contacts rather than individual hold events.
metrics.action: Read with hold duration and hold disconnects.

metrics.label: Disconnected on hold · primary
metrics.meaning: Primary inbound legs disconnected in a hold state after agent connection. May include agent and customer disconnects; do not describe all of these as customer abandonment.
metrics.action: Review disconnect reason and hold experience. Never add to pre-answer queue abandonment.

metrics.label: Agent offers not accepted
metrics.meaning: Unaccepted routing attempts. The same contact may be offered multiple times and later answered. This is not a count of missed customer calls.
metrics.action: Review agent readiness, devices and routing; do not subtract from incoming calls.
metrics.time_basis: Agent activity event interval; routing-attempt grain.

metrics.label: Agent offer acceptance rate
metrics.meaning: Amazon's native answer rate for offers to agents. Offer-attempt grain, not the primary caller answer rate.
metrics.action: Investigate unaccepted offers alongside routing and device issues.
metrics.time_basis: Agent activity event interval; routing-attempt grain.

metrics.label: Transferred out · primary
metrics.meaning: Native transfer-out count on primary inbound contact legs. A transfer is not inherently a failure.
metrics.action: Review avoidable handoffs and destination staffing; do not assume internal plus external is always exhaustive.

metrics.label: Transferred out of queue
metrics.meaning: Native queue transfer-out diagnostic across eligible voice origins. Related to queue demand but not a guaranteed remainder of queued minus handled minus abandoned.
metrics.action: Inspect overflow routing and destination wait times.

reconciliations.caveat: Remainder is derived on the same contact-record reporting scope; equality alone does not prove a unique-caller or initiation cohort.
